q:
The statement (¬p) ⇒ (¬q) is logically equivalent to which of the statements below?
I. p ⇒ q
II. q ⇒ p
III. (¬q) ∨ p
IV. (¬p) ∨ q
exp:
(¬p) ⇒ (¬q) ka matlab hai ¬(¬p) ∨ (¬q) = p ∨ ¬q.
Ye contrapositive form hai: (¬p ⇒ ¬q) ≡ (q ⇒ p). So II sahi.
III: (¬q) ∨ p = p ∨ ¬q, bilkul same expression. So III bhi sahi.
I: p ⇒ q = ¬p ∨ q, ye alag hai (p=1, q=0 pe differ karta hai).
IV: (¬p) ∨ q = p ⇒ q, wahi I hai, isliye galat.
Trap: ¬p ⇒ ¬q ko p ⇒ q samajh lena (ye inverse hai, equivalent nahi).
Answer: II and III only → (D).

q:
Consider the first-order logic sentence F: ∀x(∃y R(x, y)). Assuming non-empty logical domains, which of the sentences below are implied by F?
I. ∃y(∃x R(x, y))
II. ∃y(∀x R(x, y))
III. ∀y(∃x R(x, y))
IV. ¬∃x(∀y ¬R(x, y))
exp:
F kehta hai: har x ke liye koi y hai jisse R(x,y) true.
I: domain non-empty hai, to koi x lo, uske liye y milega → ∃x∃y R(x,y) true. I implied.
IV: ¬∃x∀y¬R(x,y) ≡ ∀x∃y R(x,y) = F itself. IV implied.
II: ∃y∀x R(x,y) ek hi common y maangta hai sab x ke liye — F se nahi aata (quantifier swap galat).
III: ∀y∃x R(x,y) — har y kisi x se related ho, ye bhi guarantee nahi.
Counter-example: domain {1,2}, R(x,y) iff x=y → F true, II false; R = {(1,1),(2,1)} → F true, III false.
Answer: I and IV only → (B).

q:
Let c₁, …, cₙ be scalars, not all zero, such that ∑ᵢ₌₁ⁿ cᵢaᵢ = 0 where aᵢ are column vectors in Rⁿ.
Consider the set of linear equations
Ax = b
where A = [a₁, …, aₙ] and b = ∑ᵢ₌₁ⁿ aᵢ. The set of equations has
opts: a unique solution at x = Jₙ where Jₙ denotes an n-dimensional vector of all 1
exp:
∑cᵢaᵢ = 0 with c not all zero → columns linearly dependent → rank(A) < n.
b = ∑aᵢ = A·Jₙ, to x = Jₙ ek solution hai, system consistent hai.
Ac = 0 with c ≠ 0, to null space non-trivial hai.
x = Jₙ + t·c har real t ke liye solution hai.
Consistent + non-trivial null space → infinitely many solutions.
Trap: x = Jₙ solution to hai, par unique nahi.
Answer: (C).

q:
Consider the following functions from positive integers to real numbers:
10, √n, n, log₂n, 100/n.
The CORRECT arrangement of the above functions in increasing order of asymptotic complexity is:
exp:
100/n → n badhne par 0 ki taraf jata hai, sabse slow.
10 → constant, Θ(1).
log₂n → slowly badhta hai, par constant se bada.
√n = n^0.5 → log n se asymptotically bada.
n → sabse bada.
Order: 100/n < 10 < log₂n < √n < n.
Trap: 100/n ko constant 10 se bada samajhna (chhote n pe bada dikhta hai, par asymptotically chhota hai).
Answer: (B).

q:
Consider the following table:
Algorithms | Design Paradigms
(P) Kruskal | (i) Divide and Conquer
(Q) Quicksort | (ii) Greedy
(R) Floyd-Warshall | (iii) Dynamic Programming
Match the algorithms to the design paradigms they are based on.
exp:
Kruskal: har step pe sabse chhota safe edge choose karta hai → Greedy (ii).
Quicksort: pivot se partition, phir dono halves recursively sort → Divide and Conquer (i).
Floyd-Warshall: d_k(i,j) = min(d_{k−1}(i,j), d_{k−1}(i,k) + d_{k−1}(k,j)) → Dynamic Programming (iii).
So P↔ii, Q↔i, R↔iii.
Answer: (C).

q:
Let T be a binary search tree with 15 nodes. The minimum and maximum possible heights of T are:
Note: The height of a tree with a single node is 0.
exp:
Height h wale binary tree me max nodes = 2^(h+1) − 1.
15 = 2⁴ − 1 → h = 3 pe complete tree me exactly 15 nodes aa jate hain. Minimum height = 3.
Maximum height: skewed tree (chain) — 15 nodes, 14 edges → height 14.
Note: single node ki height 0 di hai, isliye edges count karo.
Trap: height ko nodes count karke 4 aur 15 likh dena.
Answer: 3 and 14 → (B).

q: The n-bit fixed-point representation of an unsigned real number X uses f bits for the fraction part. Let i = n − f. The range of decimal values for X in this representation is
exp:
i integer bits, f fraction bits, unsigned.
Minimum: sab bits 0 → X = 0.
Maximum: sab bits 1 → integer part = 2ⁱ − 1, fraction part = 1 − 2⁻ᶠ.
Total max = 2ⁱ − 1 + 1 − 2⁻ᶠ = 2ⁱ − 2⁻ᶠ.
Trap: minimum ko 2⁻ᶠ lena — all-zero pattern bhi valid hai, jo 0 deta hai.
Answer: 0 to (2ⁱ − 2⁻ᶠ) → (D).

q:
Consider the C code fragment given below.
Assuming that m and n point to valid NULL-terminated linked lists, invocation of join will
opts: append list m to the end of list n for all inputs.
either cause a null pointer dereference or append list m to the end of list n.
cause a null pointer dereference for all inputs.
append list n to the end of list m for all inputs.
exp:
p = n se start, last node tak jate hain, phir p->next = m → list m, list n ke end me append hoti hai.
Par agar n empty list hai (n == NULL), to p->next pehli hi baar NULL dereference karega.
Valid NULL-terminated list empty bhi ho sakti hai.
To ya to null pointer dereference, ya m append at end of n.
Trap: 'for all inputs' wala option (A) — empty n ka case miss ho jata hai.
Answer: (B).

q:
When two 8-bit numbers A₇⋯A₀ and B₇⋯B₀ in 2's complement representation (with A₀ and B₀ as the least significant bits) are added using a ripple-carry adder, the sum bits obtained are S₇⋯S₀ and the carry bits are C₇⋯C₀. An overflow is said to have occurred if
(Here X' denotes the complement of X.)
opts: all the carry bits (C₇, ⋯, C₀) are 1
exp:
2's complement me overflow tab hota hai jab dono operands same sign ke hon aur result ka sign alag ho.
Sign bits: A₇, B₇, S₇.
Dono negative (A₇ = B₇ = 1) aur result positive (S₇ = 0) → A₇·B₇·S₇'.
Dono positive (A₇ = B₇ = 0) aur result negative (S₇ = 1) → A₇'·B₇'·S₇.
Overflow = A₇B₇S₇' + A₇'B₇'S₇.
Trap: sirf carry-out C₇ = 1 ko overflow maan lena — wo unsigned overflow hai, signed nahi.
Answer: (C).

q:
Consider the following context-free grammar over the alphabet Σ = {a, b, c} with S as the start symbol:
Which one of the following represents the language generated by the above grammar?
code:
S → abScT | abcT
T → bT | b
opts: {(ab)ⁿ cb^m₁ cb^m₂ … cb^mₙ | n, m₁, m₂, …, mₙ ≥ 1}
exp:
T → bT | b generates bᵐ, m ≥ 1.
S → abScT ko (n−1) baar use karo, phir S → abcT.
Result: (ab)ⁿ cT cT … cT, total n baar 'cT'.
Har T independently b^mᵢ generate karta hai (mᵢ ≥ 1 alag-alag ho sakte hain).
So string = (ab)ⁿ cb^m₁ cb^m₂ … cb^mₙ.
Trap: option (C) sab T ko same m maan leta hai — galat, har T independent hai.
Answer: (B).

q:
Consider the C struct defined below:
The base address of student is available in register R1. The field student.grade can be accessed efficiently using
opts: Index addressing mode, X(R1), where X is an offset represented in 2's complement 16-bit representation.
exp:
grade field struct ke base se fixed offset pe hai (marks[100] ke baad, e.g. 100 × 4 = 400 bytes).
R1 me base address hai, to effective address = R1 + constant offset.
Ye exactly index / base-displacement addressing X(R1) hai.
(R1)+ ya −(R1) sirf R1 ya uske paas ka address dete hain, grade tak nahi pahunchte.
Register direct R1 to R1 ki value hi deta hai, memory field nahi.
Answer: (D).

q:
Consider the following intermediate program in three address code
Which one of the following corresponds to a static single assignment form of the above code?
code:
p = a - b
q = p * c
p = u * v
q = p + q
opts:
p₁ = a − b
q₁ = p₁ * c
p₁ = u * v
q₁ = p₁ + q₁

p₃ = a − b
q₄ = p₃ * c
p₄ = u * v
q₅ = p₄ + q₄

p₁ = a − b
q₁ = p₂ * c
p₃ = u * v
q₂ = p₄ + q₃

p₁ = a − b
q₁ = p * c
p₂ = u * v
q₂ = p + q
exp:
SSA rule: har variable ko exactly ek baar assign karo, aur har use sahi (latest) version ko refer kare.
(A): p₁ aur q₁ do baar assign → SSA nahi.
(C): q₁ = p₂ * c, par p₂ kabhi define hi nahi hua → galat.
(D): q₁ = p * c me unversioned p use ho raha hai → galat.
(B): p₃, q₄, p₄, q₅ sab ek-ek baar assign; q₄ = p₃*c aur q₅ = p₄+q₄ sahi versions use karte hain.
Subscript numbers kuch bhi ho sakte hain, bas unique hone chahiye.
Answer: (B).

q:
Consider the following C code:
The code suffers from which one of the following problems:
opts: compiler error as the return of malloc is not typecast appropriately
compiler error because the comparison should be made as x == NULL and not as shown
compiles successfully but execution may result in dangling pointer
compiles successfully but execution may result in memory leak
exp:
C me malloc ka void* implicitly int* me convert ho jata hai → (A) galat.
NULL == x bhi valid comparison hai → (B) galat.
Pehla malloc x ko block-1 deta hai. assignval(x,0) wahi pointer return karta hai (non-NULL), to if(x) true.
Ab x = malloc(...) naya block-2 deta hai — block-1 ka address kho gaya, kabhi free nahi hoga.
End me free(x) sirf block-2 free karta hai → memory leak.
Koi freed memory use nahi ho rahi, isliye dangling pointer nahi.
Answer: (D).

q: Consider a TCP client and a TCP server running on two different machines. After completing data transfer, the TCP client calls close to terminate the connection and a FIN segment is sent to the TCP server. Server-side TCP responds by sending an ACK, which is received by the client-side TCP. As per the TCP connection state diagram (RFC 793), in which state does the client-side TCP connection wait for the FIN from the server-side TCP?
exp:
Client close() call karta hai, FIN bhejta hai → ESTABLISHED se FIN-WAIT-1.
Server ka ACK aata hai → client FIN-WAIT-2 me chala jata hai.
FIN-WAIT-2 me client server ke FIN ka wait karta hai.
Server ka FIN aane par client ACK bhejta hai aur TIME-WAIT me jata hai.
LAST-ACK server (passive closer) side ki state hai.
Answer: FIN-WAIT-2 → (D).

q:
A sender S sends a message m to receiver R, which is digitally signed by S with its private key. In this scenario, one or more of the following security violations can take place.
(I) S can launch a birthday attack to replace m with a fraudulent message.
(II) A third party attacker can launch a birthday attack to replace m with a fraudulent message.
(III) R can launch a birthday attack to replace m with a fraudulent message.
Which of the following are possible security violations?
exp:
Birthday attack: do alag messages dhundhna jinka hash same ho (collision), jo ~2^(n/2) effort me possible hai.
Sender S khud do messages m aur m' bana sakta hai with H(m) = H(m'), ek pe sign karke baad me doosra claim kar sakta hai → I possible.
Third party ya R ke paas S ki private key nahi hai; unhe ek given m ke liye second pre-image chahiye, jo birthday attack se nahi milta.
Isliye sirf S hi birthday attack se m replace kar sakta hai.
Trap: birthday attack ko 'kisi bhi attacker' ka tool samajhna — yahan collision pair pehle se chunna padta hai, jo sirf signer kar sakta hai.
Answer: (I) only → (B).

q:
The following functional dependencies hold true for the relational schema R{V, W, X, Y, Z}:
V → W
VW → X
Y → VX
Y → Z
Which of the following is irreducible equivalent for this set of functional dependencies?
opts:
V → W
V → X
Y → V
Y → Z

V → W
W → X
Y → V
Y → Z

V → W
V → X
Y → V
Y → X
Y → Z

V → W
W → X
Y → V
Y → X
Y → Z
exp:
Step 1 (split RHS): V→W, VW→X, Y→V, Y→X, Y→Z.
Step 2 (extraneous LHS): VW→X me V⁺ = {V,W,X} → W extraneous, to V→X.
Step 3 (redundant FD): Y→X, Y→V aur V→X se derive hota hai → hata do.
Baaki: V→W, V→X, Y→V, Y→Z — koi redundant nahi.
(B)/(D) me W→X hai, jo original se derive nahi hota (W⁺ = {W}).
(C) me Y→X redundant hai, isliye irreducible nahi.
Answer: (A).

q:
Consider the following grammar:
What is FOLLOW(Q)?
code:
P → xQRS
Q → yz | z
R → w | ε
S → y
exp:
Q sirf P → xQRS me aata hai, uske baad RS hai.
FOLLOW(Q) ⊇ FIRST(RS).
FIRST(R) = {w, ε}. R nullable hai, isliye FIRST(S) bhi add karo.
FIRST(S) = {y}.
So FIRST(RS) = {w, y}; S nullable nahi, to FOLLOW(P) (= {$}) add nahi hota.
Trap: {R} — FOLLOW me terminals hote hain, non-terminals nahi.
Answer: {w, y} → (C).

q: Threads of a process share
exp:
Ek process ke sab threads same address space share karte hain.
Shared: code section, data section (global/static variables), heap, open files.
Private per thread: stack, registers, program counter.
To globals aur heap dono shared hain.
Answer: (D).

q: Let X be a Gaussian random variable with mean 0 and variance σ². Let Y = max(X, 0) where max(a, b) is the maximum of a and b. The median of Y is ______.
exp:
X ~ N(0, σ²), symmetric about 0 → P(X ≤ 0) = 0.5.
Y = max(X,0): X ≤ 0 hone par Y = 0, warna Y = X > 0.
P(Y = 0) = 0.5, aur P(Y ≤ y) = P(X ≤ y) for y ≥ 0.
Median m: P(Y ≤ m) ≥ 0.5 aur P(Y ≥ m) ≥ 0.5.
m = 0 pe: P(Y ≤ 0) = 0.5, P(Y ≥ 0) = 1 → dono conditions satisfy.
Answer: 0.

q: Let T be a tree with 10 vertices. The sum of the degrees of all the vertices in T is ______.
exp:
n vertices wale tree me edges = n − 1 = 9.
Handshaking lemma: sum of degrees = 2 × edges.
Sum = 2 × 9 = 18.
Answer: 18.

q:
Consider the Karnaugh map given below, where X represents "don't care" and blank represents 0.
Assume for all inputs (a, b, c, d), the respective complements (a', b', c', d') are also available. The above logic is implemented using 2-input NOR gates only. The minimum number of gates required is ______.
code:
K-map: rows = dc, columns = ba (Gray order)
        ba=00  ba=01  ba=11  ba=10
dc=00     0      X      X      0
dc=01     1      0      0      X
dc=11     1      0      0      1
dc=10     0      X      X      0
exp:
1s: (dc=01, ba=00), (dc=11, ba=00), (dc=11, ba=10); X at (dc=01, ba=10).
In sab cells me c = 1 aur a = 0 hai.
c=1, a=0 wale exactly 4 cells hain (rows 01 & 11, cols 00 & 10) — teen 1 aur ek X → ek quad.
Baaki X (a=1 wale) ko 0 treat karo.
f = c·a' = (c' + a)' = NOR(c', a).
c' available hai, to sirf ek 2-input NOR gate chahiye.
Answer: 1.

q: Consider the language L given by the regular expression (a + b)* b (a + b) over the alphabet {a, b}. The smallest number of states needed in a deterministic finite-state automaton (DFA) accepting L is ______.
exp:
L = strings jinka second-last symbol b hai.
DFA ko last 2 symbols yaad rakhne padte hain: aa, ab, ba, bb → 4 states.
Accepting: ba aur bb (second-last = b).
Ye 4 states distinguishable hain (Myhill-Nerode: suffixes ε aur 'a' se alag kar sakte hain).
General rule: 'k-th symbol from end' ke liye minimal DFA = 2ᵏ states; k = 2 → 4.
Answer: 4.

q:
Consider a database that has the relation schema EMP (EmpId, EmpName, and DeptName). An instance of the schema EMP and a SQL query on it are given below.
The output of executing the SQL query is ______.
code:
EMP
EmpId  EmpName  DeptName
1      XYA      AA
2      XYB      AA
3      XYC      AA
4      XYD      AA
5      XYE      AB
6      XYF      AB
7      XYG      AB
8      XYH      AC
9      XYI      AC
10     XYJ      AC
11     XYK      AD
12     XYL      AD
13     XYM      AE

SELECT AVG(EC.Num)
FROM EC
WHERE (DeptName, Num) IN
      (SELECT DeptName, COUNT(EmpId) AS
                        EC(DeptName, Num)
       FROM EMP
       GROUP BY DeptName)
exp:
Inner query har department ke employees count karti hai: EC(DeptName, Num).
AA = 4, AB = 3, AC = 3, AD = 2, AE = 1.
Outer query in sab (DeptName, Num) rows ka AVG(Num) nikalti hai.
Sum = 4 + 3 + 3 + 2 + 1 = 13, departments = 5.
AVG = 13/5 = 2.6.
Answer: 2.6.

q:
Consider the following CPU processes with arrival times (in milliseconds) and length of CPU bursts (in milliseconds) as given below:
Process | Arrival time | Burst time
P1 | 0 | 7
P2 | 3 | 3
P3 | 5 | 5
P4 | 6 | 2
If the pre-emptive shortest remaining time first scheduling algorithm is used to schedule the processes, then the average waiting time across all processes is ______ milliseconds.
exp:
0–3: P1 chalta hai (remaining 4).
t=3: P2 (3) < P1 (4) → P2 3–6. t=5 pe P3 (5) aaya, P2 ka rem 1 hai, wahi chalta rahega.
t=6: P1 = 4, P3 = 5, P4 = 2 → P4 6–8.
t=8: P1 (4) → 8–12. Phir P3 12–17.
Waiting = completion − arrival − burst: P1 = 12−0−7 = 5, P2 = 6−3−3 = 0, P3 = 17−5−5 = 7, P4 = 8−6−2 = 0.
Average = 12/4 = 3.
Answer: 3 ms.

q: Consider a two-level cache hierarchy with L1 and L2 caches. An application incurs 1.4 memory accesses per instruction on average. For this application, the miss rate of L1 cache is 0.1; the L2 cache experiences, on average, 7 misses per 1000 instructions. The miss rate of L2 expressed correct to two decimal places is ______.
exp:
1000 instructions → 1.4 × 1000 = 1400 memory accesses.
L1 misses = 0.1 × 1400 = 140 → ye sab L2 me jate hain (L2 accesses).
L2 misses = 7 (per 1000 instructions).
L2 (local) miss rate = 7 / 140 = 0.05.
Trap: 7/1400 = 0.005 lena — wo global miss rate hai, L2 ka local miss rate nahi.
Answer: 0.05.

q:
Let G = (V, E) be any connected undirected edge-weighted graph. The weights of the edges in E are positive and distinct. Consider the following statements:
(I) Minimum Spanning Tree of G is always unique.
(II) Shortest path between any two vertices of G is always unique.
Which of the above statements is/are necessarily true?
exp:
(I): Distinct edge weights → MST unique hota hai (standard theorem; cut property har step pe unique light edge deta hai). True.
(II): Path weight edges ka sum hai, distinct edges ke sums equal ho sakte hain.
Example: triangle A–B = 1, B–C = 2, A–C = 3. A se C: direct = 3, A–B–C = 1 + 2 = 3 → do shortest paths.
Isliye (II) necessarily true nahi.
Trap: 'distinct weights → sab unique' — sirf MST ke liye sahi hai.
Answer: (I) only → (A).

q: A multithreaded program P executes with x number of threads and uses y number of locks for ensuring mutual exclusion while operating on shared memory locations. All locks in the program are non-reentrant, i.e., if a thread holds a lock l, then it cannot re-acquire lock l without releasing it. If a thread is unable to acquire a lock, it blocks until the lock becomes available. The minimum value of x and the minimum value of y together for which execution of P can result in a deadlock are:
exp:
Locks non-reentrant hain: jo thread lock l hold karta hai, wo dobara l acquire nahi kar sakta.
Ek thread lock l le, phir (release kiye bina) phir se lock(l) call kare.
Lock available nahi hai → thread block ho jata hai, aur release karne wala bhi wahi blocked thread hai.
Ye self-deadlock hai — sirf 1 thread aur 1 lock se.
Trap: classic 2 threads + 2 locks circular wait sochna — non-reentrant lock me 1, 1 hi kaafi hai.
Answer: x = 1, y = 1 → (D).

q: The value of lim_{x→1} (x⁷ − 2x⁵ + 1)/(x³ − 3x² + 2)
exp:
x = 1 pe numerator = 1 − 2 + 1 = 0, denominator = 1 − 3 + 2 = 0 → 0/0 form.
L'Hôpital: derivative lo.
Numerator' = 7x⁶ − 10x⁴ → x = 1 pe 7 − 10 = −3.
Denominator' = 3x² − 6x → x = 1 pe 3 − 6 = −3.
Limit = −3/−3 = 1.
Answer: 1 → (C).

q: Let p, q, and r be propositions and the expression (p → q) → r be a contradiction. Then, the expression (r → p) → q is
opts: always TRUE when p is FALSE.
always TRUE when q is TRUE.
exp:
(p → q) → r hamesha false hai → iska matlab (p → q) = T aur r = F, har valid assignment me.
r = F → (r → p) = T (false antecedent).
To (r → p) → q = T → q = q.
Expression ki value q ke barabar hai.
q TRUE → expression TRUE. q FALSE → expression FALSE, isliye tautology/contradiction nahi.
p FALSE, q FALSE (p→q = T) pe expression false → (C) galat.
Answer: (D).

q: Let u and v be two vectors in R² whose Euclidean norms satisfy ‖u‖ = 2‖v‖. What is the value of α such that w = u + αv bisects the angle between u and v?
exp:
Do vectors ka sum angle bisect karta hai jab dono ki length equal ho (rhombus ka diagonal).
Bisector direction: u/‖u‖ + v/‖v‖.
w = u + αv ko is direction me chahiye → αv ki length = ‖u‖.
α‖v‖ = ‖u‖ = 2‖v‖ → α = 2.
Check: w = u + 2v, ‖u‖ = ‖2v‖, rhombus → diagonal angle bisect karta hai.
Answer: 2 → (A).

q:
Let A be n × n real valued square symmetric matrix of rank 2 with ∑ᵢ₌₁ⁿ ∑ⱼ₌₁ⁿ Aᵢⱼ² = 50. Consider the following statements.
(I) One eigenvalue must be in [−5, 5]
(II) The eigenvalue with the largest magnitude must be strictly greater than 5
Which of the above statements about eigenvalues of A is/are necessarily CORRECT?
exp:
Symmetric A ke liye ∑Aᵢⱼ² = trace(AᵀA) = ∑λᵢ².
Rank 2 → sirf do non-zero eigenvalues λ₁, λ₂: λ₁² + λ₂² = 50.
(I): Agar dono |λ| > 5 hote to sum > 50 — impossible. To ek |λ| ≤ 5 → I true. (n > 2 ho to 0 bhi eigenvalue hai.)
(II): λ₁ = λ₂ = 5 lo: 25 + 25 = 50, largest magnitude = 5, strictly > 5 nahi. So II necessarily true nahi.
Answer: (I) only → (B).

q: A computer network uses polynomials over GF(2) for error checking with 8 bits as information bits and uses x³ + x + 1 as the generator polynomial to generate the check bits. In this network, the message 01011011 is transmitted as
exp:
Generator x³ + x + 1 = 1011 (degree 3) → 3 check bits.
Message ke peeche 3 zeros lagao: 01011011000.
Isse 1011 se mod-2 (XOR) divide karo.
1011 XOR steps: 1011→0000 ... baaki 1000 → 1000⊕1011 = 0011, phir aage bits laakar continue karo.
Final remainder = 101.
Transmitted = message + remainder = 01011011 101.
Check: 01011011101 ko 1011 se divide karne pe remainder 0 aata hai.
Answer: (C).

q:
Consider a combination of T and D flip-flops connected as shown below. The output of the D flip-flop is connected to the input of the T flip-flop and the output of the T flip-flop is connected to the input of the D flip-flop.
[Circuit: T flip-flop with output Q₁, D flip-flop with output Q₀. T input = Q₀, D input = Q₁. Both flip-flops share the same Clock.]
Initially, both Q₀ and Q₁ are set to 1 (before the 1st clock cycle). The outputs
opts: Q₁Q₀ after the 3rd cycle are 11 and after the 4th cycle are 00 respectively
Q₁Q₀ after the 3rd cycle are 11 and after the 4th cycle are 01 respectively
Q₁Q₀ after the 3rd cycle are 00 and after the 4th cycle are 11 respectively
Q₁Q₀ after the 3rd cycle are 01 and after the 4th cycle are 01 respectively
exp:
T = Q₀ → Q₁(next) = Q₁ ⊕ Q₀. D = Q₁ → Q₀(next) = Q₁ (purana Q₁).
Start Q₁Q₀ = 11.
Cycle 1: Q₁ = 1⊕1 = 0, Q₀ = 1 → 01.
Cycle 2: Q₁ = 0⊕1 = 1, Q₀ = 0 → 10.
Cycle 3: Q₁ = 1⊕0 = 1, Q₀ = 1 → 11.
Cycle 4: Q₁ = 1⊕1 = 0, Q₀ = 1 → 01.
Trap: D ko naya Q₁ de dena — dono flip-flops same clock edge pe purani values use karte hain.
Answer: 11 and 01 → (B).

q:
If G is a grammar with productions
S → SaS | aSb | bSa | SS | ε
where S is the start variable, then which one of the following strings is not generated by G?
exp:
Har production me #a ≥ #b maintain hota hai: aSb, bSa balanced add karte hain, SaS ek extra a add karta hai.
Isliye G ki har string me #a ≥ #b.
babba: a = 2, b = 3 → #a < #b → generate nahi ho sakta.
Baaki check: abab = SS with S→aSb (ab)(ab). aaab = SaS se a, a extra + ab. abbaa = (ab)(ba)(a) via SS aur SaS.
Answer: babba → (D).

q:
Consider the following two functions.
The output printed when fun1(5) is called is
exp:
fun1(5): print 5 → fun2(3): print 3 → fun1(4) (n ab 4): print 4 → fun2(2): print 2 → fun1(3): print 3 → fun2(1): print 1 → fun1(2): print 2 → fun2(0) return.
Ab unwind: fun1(2) print 2.
fun2(1) me n = 2 ho chuka (++n) → print 2.
fun1(3) print 3; fun2(2) me n = 3 → print 3.
fun1(4) print 4; fun2(3) me n = 4 → print 4; fun1(5) print 5.
Output: 5 3 4 2 3 1 2 | 2 2 3 3 4 4 5 = 53423122233445.
Trap: fun2 me ++n ke baad n change ho jata hai — second printf naya value print karta hai.
Answer: (A).

q:
Consider the C functions foo and bar given below:
Invocations of foo(3) and bar(3) will result in :
opts: Infinite loop and abnormal termination respectively.
Abnormal termination and infinite loop respectively.
exp:
foo(3): foo(val--) post-decrement hai, to call foo(3) hi hota hai (val baad me 2 hota hai).
foo(3) → foo(3) → foo(3) ... infinite recursion → stack overflow → abnormal termination.
bar(3): bar(2) → bar(1) → bar(0) returns 0.
bar(1) me val = 1 kabhi change nahi hota → while(val > 0) hamesha true, bar(0) baar-baar call hota hai aur return karta hai.
Stack nahi badhta, to infinite loop.
Answer: abnormal termination and infinite loop → (C).

q:
Consider the context-free grammars over the alphabet {a, b, c} given below. S and T are non-terminals.
G₁: S → aSb | T, T → cT | ε
G₂: S → bSa | T, T → cT | ε
The language L(G₁) ∩ L(G₂) is
exp:
L(G₁) = { aⁿ cᵐ bⁿ | n, m ≥ 0 }.
L(G₂) = { bⁿ cᵐ aⁿ | n, m ≥ 0 }.
Common string: G₁ strings a se start (ya c/ε), G₂ strings b se start. Dono me hone ke liye n = 0 hona chahiye.
Intersection = { cᵐ | m ≥ 0 } = c*.
c* infinite hai par regular.
Answer: (B).

q:
Consider the following languages over the alphabet Σ = {a, b, c}.
Let L₁ = { aⁿbⁿcᵐ | m, n ≥ 0 } and L₂ = { aᵐbⁿcⁿ | m, n ≥ 0 }.
Which of the following are context-free languages?
I. L₁ ∪ L₂
II. L₁ ∩ L₂
exp:
L₁ aur L₂ dono CFL hain (ek stack se count match hota hai).
I: CFLs union ke under closed hain → L₁ ∪ L₂ CFL (S → S₁ | S₂).
II: L₁ ∩ L₂ = { aⁿbⁿcⁿ | n ≥ 0 }, jo pumping lemma se CFL nahi hai.
CFLs intersection ke under closed nahi hain — ye classic example hai.
Answer: I only → (A).

q: Let A and B be finite alphabets and let # be a symbol outside both A and B. Let f be a total function from A* to B*. We say f is computable if there exists a Turing machine M which given an input x in A*, always halts with f(x) on its tape. Let L_f denote the language { x#f(x) | x ∈ A* }. Which of the following statements is true:
opts: f is computable if and only if L_f is recursive.
f is computable if and only if L_f is recursively enumerable.
If f is computable then L_f is recursive, but not conversely.
If f is computable then L_f is recursively enumerable, but not conversely.
exp:
(⇒) f computable: input x#y lo, M se f(x) compute karo (halts), y se compare karo → accept/reject. L_f recursive.
(⇐) L_f recursive (even RE kaafi hai): x diya ho to B* ke strings y ko ek-ek karke (length order) try karo, check karo x#y ∈ L_f.
f total hai, to f(x) kisi finite step pe milega; decider har check pe halt karta hai → f computable.
So f computable ⇔ L_f recursive.
(B) bhi sahi lagta hai par RE se dovetailing chahiye; option (A) exact iff statement hai jo key me hai.
Trap: (C) — converse bhi true hai, isliye 'not conversely' galat.
Answer: (A).

q:
Recall that Belady's anomaly is that the page-fault rate may increase as the number of allocated frames increases. Now, consider the following statements:
S1: Random page replacement algorithm (where a page chosen at random is replaced) suffers from Belady's anomaly
S2: LRU page replacement algorithm suffers from Belady's anomaly
Which of the following is CORRECT?
opts: S1 is true, S2 is true
S1 is true, S2 is false
S1 is false, S2 is true
S1 is false, S2 is false
exp:
LRU ek stack algorithm hai: n frames ka page set hamesha n+1 frames ke set ka subset hota hai → faults kabhi nahi badhte. S2 false.
Random replacement stack property guarantee nahi karta.
Random choice exactly FIFO jaisa bhi behave kar sakta hai, aur FIFO me Belady's anomaly hota hai.
Isliye random bhi anomaly suffer kar sakta hai. S1 true.
Answer: S1 true, S2 false → (B).

Safe TRC query = jiska result finite ho aur values database ke domain se hi aayein.
Teeno queries me t[EmpName] ko EMP ke kisi tuple u se bind kiya gaya hai, to t ke values unbounded domain se nahi aate.
Intended reading: t EMP ke tuples (u) par range karta hai, aur DeptId condition sirf filter hai (DEPT me hai ya nahi).
(I) = employees jinka DeptId kisi DEPT me nahi (NULL waale bhi), (II) = jinka DeptId kisi dept se alag hai, (III) = valid dept waale employees.
Har case me result EMP ke finite tuples ka subset hai → teeno safe.
Note: official key (D) deta hai; strict reading me t[DeptId] ko unbounded maana ja sakta hai, par exam ka intended answer ye hai.
Answer: (I), (II) and (III) → (D).

q:
In a database system, unique timestamps are assigned to each transaction using Lamport's logical clock. Let TS(T₁) and TS(T₂) be the timestamps of transactions T₁ and T₂ respectively. Besides, T₁ holds a lock on the resource R, and T₂ has requested a conflicting lock on the same resource R. The following algorithm is used to prevent deadlocks in the database system assuming that a killed transaction is restarted with the same timestamp.
if TS(T₂) < TS(T₁) then
    T₁ is killed
else T₂ waits.
Assume any transaction that is not killed terminates eventually. Which of the following is TRUE about the database system that uses the above algorithm to prevent deadlocks?
opts: The database system is both deadlock-free and starvation-free.
The database system is deadlock-free, but not starvation-free.
The database system is starvation-free, but not deadlock-free.
The database system is neither deadlock-free nor starvation-free.
exp:
T₂ requester hai, T₁ holder. Chhota timestamp = older.
Requester older ho (TS(T₂) < TS(T₁)) → holder (younger) killed; warna requester (younger) wait karta hai. Ye wound-wait scheme hai.
Wait sirf younger → older direction me hota hai, to wait-for graph me cycle nahi ban sakta → deadlock-free.
Killed transaction same timestamp ke saath restart hota hai, to time ke saath wo sabse purana ban jata hai.
Sabse purane transaction ko koi kill nahi kar sakta, wo eventually complete hoga → starvation-free.
Answer: (A).

q:
Consider the following grammar:
where relop is a relational operator (e.g., <, >, …), ε refers to the empty statement, and if, then, else are terminals.
Consider a program P following the above grammar containing ten if terminals. The number of control flow paths in P is ______. For example, the program
if e₁ then e₂ else e₃
has 2 control flow paths, e₁ → e₂ and e₁ → e₃.
code:
stmt   -> if expr then expr else expr; stmt | ε
expr   -> term relop term | term
term   -> id | number
id     -> a | b | c
number -> [0-9]
exp:
Grammar me if-statements nested nahi ho sakte (then/else ke andar sirf expr hai), sirf sequence me aate hain.
To P = 10 if-then-else statements ek ke baad ek.
Har if ke 2 paths (then ya else), aur choices independent hain.
Total paths = 2 × 2 × … (10 baar) = 2¹⁰ = 1024.
Trap: nested samajhkar 11 ya 20 count karna — yahan sequential hai, isliye multiply hota hai.
Answer: 1024.

q: In a RSA cryptosystem, a participant A uses two prime numbers p = 13 and q = 17 to generate her public and private keys. If the public key of A is 35, then the private key of A is ______.

The values of parameters for the Stop-and-Wait ARQ protocol are as given below:
Bit rate of the transmission channel = 1 Mbps.
Propagation delay from sender to receiver = 0.75 ms.
Time to process a frame = 0.25 ms.
Number of bytes in the information frame = 1980.
Number of bytes in the acknowledge frame = 20.
Number of overhead bytes in the information frame = 20.
Assume that there are no transmission errors. Then, the transmission efficiency (expressed in percentage) of the Stop-and-Wait ARQ protocol for the above parameters is ______ (correct to 2 decimal places).
exp:
Frame transmission = 1980×8 / 10⁶ = 15.84 ms.
ACK transmission = 20×8 / 10⁶ = 0.16 ms.
Round-trip propagation = 2 × 0.75 = 1.5 ms. Processing = 0.25 ms.
Total cycle = 15.84 + 0.16 + 1.5 + 0.25 = 17.75 ms.
Useful data = 1980 − 20 = 1960 bytes → 1960×8 / 10⁶ = 15.68 ms.
Efficiency = 15.68 / 17.75 ≈ 88.34%.
(Agar processing dono ends pe 0.25+0.25 lo to 15.68/18 = 87.11% — key range 86.5–89.5 dono ko cover karta hai.)
Trap: overhead bytes ko useful data me gin lena.
Answer: ≈ 88.34.

q:
Consider a database that has the relation schema CR(StudentName, CourseName). An instance of the schema CR is as given below.
The following query is made on the database.
T1 ← π_CourseName(σ_StudentName='SA'(CR))
T2 ← CR ÷ T1
The number of rows in T2 is ______.
code:
CR
StudentName  CourseName
SA           CA
SA           CB
SA           CC
SB           CB
SB           CC
SC           CA
SC           CB
SC           CC
SD           CA
SD           CB
SD           CC
SD           CD
SE           CD
SE           CA
SE           CB
SF           CA
SF           CB
SF           CC
exp:
T1 = SA ke courses = {CA, CB, CC}.
CR ÷ T1 = wo students jo CA, CB, CC teeno lete hain.
SA: CA, CB, CC ✓. SB: CA nahi ✗. SC: ✓. SD: CA, CB, CC, CD ✓ (extra course chalega).
SE: CC nahi ✗. SF: ✓.
T2 = {SA, SC, SD, SF} → 4 rows.
Answer: 4.

q: The number of integers between 1 and 500 (both inclusive) that are divisible by 3 or 5 or 7 is ______.

Let A be an array of 31 numbers consisting of a sequence of 0's followed by a sequence of 1's. The problem is to find the smallest index i such that A[i] is 1 by probing the minimum number of locations in A. The worst case number of probes performed by an optimal algorithm is ______.
exp:
Array sorted hai (0s phir 1s), to binary search optimal hai.
First 1 ki position ke possible outcomes: index 1..31 ya 'koi 1 nahi' → 32 outcomes.
Har probe outcomes ko max half karta hai → probes ≥ ⌈log₂ 32⌉ = 5.
Binary search 31 elements pe 5 probes me answer deta hai.
Answer: 5.

q:
Consider a RISC machine where each instruction is exactly 4 bytes long. Conditional and unconditional branch instructions use PC-relative addressing mode with Offset specified in bytes to the target location of the branch instruction. Further the Offset is always with respect to the address of the next instruction in the program sequence. Consider the following instruction sequence
If the target of the branch instruction is i, then the decimal value of the Offset is ______.
code:
Instr. No.    Instruction
i   :        add   R2, R3, R4
i+1 :        sub   R5, R6, R7
i+2 :        cmp   R1, R9, R10
i+3 :        beq   R1,  Offset
exp:
Instruction i ka address X lo. Har instruction 4 bytes.
beq (i+3) ka address X + 12; next instruction (i+4) ka address X + 16 → yahi PC hai.
Target = i = X.
Offset = target − PC = X − (X + 16) = −16.
Trap: beq ke apne address se measure karke −12 likh dena.
Answer: −16.

q:
Instruction execution in a processor is divided into 5 stages, Instruction Fetch (IF), Instruction Decode (ID), Operand Fetch (OF), Execute (EX), and Write Back (WB). These stages take 5, 4, 20, 10, and 3 nanoseconds (ns) respectively. A pipelined implementation of the processor requires buffering between each pair of consecutive stages with a delay of 2 ns. Two pipelined implementations of the processor are contemplated:
(i) a naive pipeline implementation (NP) with 5 stages and
(ii) an efficient pipeline (EP) where the OF stage is divided into stages OF1 and OF2 with execution times of 12 ns and 8 ns respectively.
The speedup (correct to two decimal places) achieved by EP over NP in executing 20 independent instructions with no hazards is ______.
exp:
NP: cycle time = max(5,4,20,10,3) + 2 = 22 ns, k = 5.
NP time = (k + n − 1) × cycle = (5 + 19) × 22 = 528 ns.
EP: stages 5,4,12,8,10,3 → cycle = 12 + 2 = 14 ns, k = 6.
EP time = (6 + 19) × 14 = 350 ns.
Speedup = 528 / 350 ≈ 1.51.
Trap: EP me stages 6 ho gaye — fill time me k = 6 lena mat bhoolo.
Answer: ≈ 1.51.

q:
Consider a 2-way set associative cache with 256 blocks and uses LRU replacement. Initially the cache is empty. Conflict misses are those misses which occur due to contention of multiple blocks for the same cache set. Compulsory misses occur due to first time access to the block. The following sequence of accesses to memory blocks
(0, 128, 256, 128, 0, 128, 256, 128, 1, 129, 257, 129, 1, 129, 257, 129)
is repeated 10 times. The number of conflict misses experienced by the cache is ______.
exp:
256 blocks, 2-way → 128 sets. Set = block mod 128.
Set 0: 0, 128, 256. Set 1: 1, 129, 257. Dono sets ka pattern same hai, alag-alag simulate karo.
Set 0 first pass (LRU, 2 ways): 0 M, 128 M, 256 M (0 out), 128 H, 0 M (256 out), 128 H, 256 M (0 out), 128 H → 5 misses.
Agle passes me set me {128, 256} bache hain, 0 pe miss → same pattern: 0 M, 128 H, 256 M, 128 H, 0 M, 128 H, 256 M, 128 H → 4 misses.
Set 0 total = 5 + 9×4 = 41; set 1 bhi 41 → total misses = 82.
Compulsory misses = distinct blocks = 6.
Conflict misses = 82 − 6 = 76.
Answer: 76.

q: Consider the expression (a − 1) * (((b + c) / 3) + d). Let X be the minimum number of registers required by an optimal code generation (without any register spill) algorithm for a load/store architecture, in which (i) only load and store instructions can have memory operands and (ii) arithmetic instructions can have only register or immediate operands. The value of X is ______.
exp:
Bada subtree pehle evaluate karo (Sethi-Ullman idea).
R1 ← b; R2 ← c; R1 ← R1 + R2 (b+c).
R1 ← R1 / 3 (immediate operand allowed).
R2 ← d; R1 ← R1 + R2.
R2 ← a; R2 ← R2 − 1 (immediate).
R1 ← R2 * R1.
Kabhi bhi 2 se zyada registers live nahi hue, aur b+c ke liye 2 registers zaroori hain (dono memory operands load karne padte hain).
Answer: 2.

q:
Consider the following C program.
Recall that strlen is defined in string.h as returning a value of type size_t, which is an unsigned int. The output of the program is ______.
exp:
strlen(x) = 3, strlen(y) = 5, dono unsigned (size_t).
3 − 5 unsigned arithmetic me negative nahi hota, wrap around karke bahut bada positive number banta hai (2³² − 2).
Ye c = 0 se bada hai → condition true.
len = strlen(s) = 3.
Trap: signed ki tarah −2 > 0 false maankar 5 likh dena.
Answer: 3.

q: A cache memory unit with capacity of N words and block size of B words is to be designed. If it is designed as a direct mapped cache, the length of the TAG field is 10 bits. If the cache unit is now designed as a 16-way set-associative cache, the length of the TAG field is ______ bits.
exp:
Direct mapped: address = TAG | line index (log₂(N/B)) | offset.
16-way set-associative: sets = (N/B)/16 → index bits log₂16 = 4 kam ho jate hain.
Address length same hai, offset same hai, to jo 4 bits index se hate wo TAG me chale jate hain.
TAG = 10 + 4 = 14 bits.
Answer: 14.

q: The output of executing the following C program is ______.
exp:
total(v) v ke set bits count me add karta hai; count static hai, isliye calls ke beech value retain hoti hai.
i=5 (101, 2 bits): count = 2 → x = 2.
i=4 (100, 1 bit): count = 3 → x = 5.
i=3 (11, 2 bits): count = 5 → x = 10.
i=2 (10, 1 bit): count = 6 → x = 16.
i=1 (1, 1 bit): count = 7 → x = 23.
Trap: count ko har call pe 0 se shuru maanna — static hone ki wajah se cumulative hai.
Answer: 23.

q: After Rajendra Chola returned from his voyage to Indonesia, he ______ to visit the temple in Thanjavur.
exp:
Sentence ka pehla part simple past me hai: 'returned'.
Wish lautne ke baad hua, to sequence ke hisaab se simple past chahiye.
'had wished' past perfect hai — ye lautne se pehle ka action dikhata, jo meaning ke khilaf hai.
'is wishing' present hai, galat; 'was wishing' — wish stative verb hai, continuous me awkward.
Answer: wished → (C).

q: Research in the workplace reveals that people work for many reasons ______.
exp:
'Besides' = 'in addition to / apart from'.
'Beside' = 'next to' (position).
Matlab: log paise ke alawa bhi kai reasons se kaam karte hain.
Preposition noun se pehle aata hai → 'besides money'.
Trap: beside aur besides ka confusion.
Answer: (D).

q: Rahul, Murali, Srinivas and Arul are seated around a square table. Rahul is sitting to the left of Murali. Srinivas is sitting to the right of Arul. Which of the following pairs are seated opposite each other?
exp:
Square table ke 4 seats clockwise 1, 2, 3, 4 lo; sab center ki taraf face kar rahe hain, to kisi ka 'left' = uska clockwise-next neighbour (convention fix karo).
Rahul Murali ke left me: Murali = 1, Rahul = 2.
Srinivas Arul ke right me → Arul, Srinivas ka left hai, yaani Arul = Srinivas ka clockwise-next.
Bache seats 3, 4: Srinivas = 3, Arul = 4.
Opposite pairs: 1–3 = Murali–Srinivas, 2–4 = Rahul–Arul.
Doosra convention lene par bhi mirror image aati hai, pairs same rehte hain.
Answer: Srinivas and Murali → (C).

q: Find the smallest number y such that y × 162 is a perfect cube.
exp:
162 = 2 × 81 = 2¹ × 3⁴.
Perfect cube ke liye har prime ki power 3 ka multiple honi chahiye.
2¹ → 2³ ke liye 2² chahiye. 3⁴ → 3⁶ ke liye 3² chahiye.
y = 2² × 3² = 4 × 9 = 36.
Check: 36 × 162 = 5832 = 18³ ✓.
Answer: 36 → (D).

q: The probability that a k-digit number does NOT contain the digits 0, 5, or 9 is
exp:
Har digit ke 10 choices hain (0–9).
0, 5, 9 ke alawa allowed digits = 7.
Ek digit ke liye probability = 7/10 = 0.7.
k digits independent → 0.7ᵏ.
(Leading digit ki subtlety ignore karke intended answer yahi hai.)
Answer: (C).

q:
"The hold of the nationalist imagination on our colonial past is such that anything inadequately or improperly nationalist is just not history."
Which of the following statements best reflects the author's opinion?
opts: History is viewed through the filter of nationalism.
Nationalism has to be both adequately and properly imagined.
exp:
Author keh raha hai ki nationalist soch ka colonial past pe itna asar hai ki jo cheez 'kaafi nationalist' nahi, use history hi nahi maana jata.
Matlab history ko nationalism ke lens/filter se dekha ja raha hai.
(A) imagination ka literal meaning le raha hai — galat.
(C) extreme aur unsupported hai.
(D) author ki criticism ko ulta recommendation bana deta hai.
Answer: (B).

q: Six people are seated around a circular table. There are at least two men and two women. There are at least three right-handed persons. Every woman has a left-handed person to her immediate right. None of the women are right-handed. The number of women at the table is
exp:
Women right-handed nahi → sab women left-handed.
At least 3 right-handed → wo sab men hain → men ≥ 3, to women ≤ 3.
Har woman ke immediate right me left-handed person chahiye.
Agar 3 women + 3 right-handed men ho, to left-handed sirf 3 women hain; har woman ke right me ek woman chahiye → teeno women ek cycle banayengi, jo 6 seats wale circle me possible nahi (women ek hi block me hongi, block ke last woman ke right me man aayega).
To women = 2: W W adjacent, pehli W ke right doosri W, doosri ke right ek left-handed man. Men = 4 (3 right + 1 left) → valid.
Answer: 2 → (A).

q: The expression ((x + y) − |x − y|) / 2 is equal to
opts: the maximum of x and y
the minimum of x and y
exp:
Case x ≥ y: |x − y| = x − y → (x + y − x + y)/2 = y = min.
Case x < y: |x − y| = y − x → (x + y − y + x)/2 = x = min.
Dono case me minimum aata hai.
Yaad rakho: max = ((x+y) + |x−y|)/2, min = ((x+y) − |x−y|)/2.
Answer: (B).

q: Arun, Gulab, Neel and Shweta must choose one shirt each from a pile of four shirts coloured red, pink, blue and white respectively. Arun dislikes the colour red and Shweta dislikes the colour white. Gulab and Neel like all the colours. In how many different ways can they choose the shirts so that no one has a shirt with a colour he or she dislikes?
exp:
Total assignments = 4! = 24.
Arun ko red mile: 3! = 6. Shweta ko white mile: 3! = 6.
Dono saath: Arun red, Shweta white → 2! = 2.
Inclusion-exclusion: bad = 6 + 6 − 2 = 10.
Valid = 24 − 10 = 14.
Answer: 14 → (D).

q:
A contour line joins locations having the same height above the mean sea level. The following is a contour plot of a geographical region. Contour lines are shown at 25 m intervals in this plot. If in a flood, the water level rises to 525 m, which of the villages P, Q, R, S, T get submerged?
[Figure: contour map. Left side: a hill with nested closed contours (labelled 500, 550); village P lies inside the innermost closed contour at the summit. Upper-left edge has open contours labelled 425 and 450. Village R lies in the low area between the left hill and the right hill. Right side: a second hill with nested closed contours (outer ring labelled 500, inner ring labelled 550 and an innermost ring); village Q is near the top-right corner on this hill's slope; village T is near the right edge just outside the ring labelled 500. Bottom-centre: a small depression with closed contours labelled 450; village S lies inside it.]
exp:
Contour interval 25 m: 425, 450, 475, 500, 525, 550, 575 …
P left hill ki chot pe innermost contour ke andar hai (550 se upar, ~575) → submerge nahi hoga.
Q right hill pe hai, official key ke hisaab se 525 se upar → safe.
R dono hills ke beech ke low region me hai (500 ke aas-paas ya neeche) → submerged.
S 450 wale depression ke andar hai → definitely submerged.
T right hill ke 500 contour ke bahar, low side pe hai → submerged.
Trap: contour ke label ko point ki exact height maan lena — point do contours ke beech hota hai.
Answer: R, S, T → (C).
